```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load-model}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Glerum_2018_gabapentin"))
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`

**Read this first.** The parameter values Glerum 2018 publishes (Table 3) do
not reproduce the paper's own data. Simulated from those values, gabapentin
peak concentration and AUC are about half of what the study observed, and the
typical terminal half-life (2.8 h) is about a third of the observed mean (8.2
h). The model is packaged as published, with
nothing adjusted, so that the published estimates are available and the
discrepancy can be examined. It should not be used to predict gabapentin
exposure without that in mind. The sections
[Typical-value checks](#typical-value-checks) and
[Comparison with the observed NCA](#comparison-with-the-observed-nca) quantify
the gap.

Glerum 2018 re-analysed a four-way crossover comparative bioavailability study
of oral 800 mg immediate-release gabapentin: the originator and three generic
formulations registered as bioequivalent in the Netherlands, one per period, in
24 healthy volunteers. The analysis was nonparametric (Pmetrics 1.5, NPAG
algorithm). Its aim was a model that later simulations could use to look for
individuals whose exposure changes by more than the 80-125% bioequivalence
margin when they switch formulation.

The final model (Equation 3) has two compartments, first-order absorption with
an absorption lag time, and an elimination rate constant proportional to
Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance (Equation 2, `Ke = Kr * CrCl`):

```
dose --(Tlag)--> depot --ka--> central <--k12/k21--> peripheral1
                                  |
                                  kel = Kr * CRCL
```

Every parameter was estimated separately for each formulation by splitting each
volunteer's four periods into four "pseudo subjects" (96 in all). Only one
pooled set of weighted medians and the between-occasion coefficients of
variation are published, so the package model carries those medians as typical
values with four-occasion inter-occasion variability and no inter-individual
variability.

```{r structure}
cat("ODE states:", paste(ui$state, collapse = " -> "), "\n")
cat("Observation:", paste(ui$predDf$var, collapse = ", "), "\n")
stopifnot(identical(ui$state, c("depot", "central", "peripheral1")))
```

# Population

From Methods ('Gabapentin pharmacokinetic data'): 24 healthy volunteers (14
female, 10 male) completed all four periods. Mean age was 35 years (range
21-55), mean body-mass index 23.6 kg/m^2 (19.9-30.0), mean body weight 71.0 kg
(52.7-97.0) and mean Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance 120 mL/min
(71.2-183.3). Plasma was sampled before the dose and at 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3,
3.5, 4, 4.5, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after it in each period; 1610
concentrations entered the analysis.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Glerum_2018_gabapentin")()$population, give.attr = FALSE)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lka` | log(0.26) 1/h | Table 3, Ka 0.26 (95% CI 0.23-0.31) |
| `ltlag` | log(0.30) h | Table 3, Tlag 0.30 (0.21-0.35) |
| `lvc` | log(90.0) L | Table 3, V 90.0 (83.5-106) |
| `lk12` | log(0.16) 1/h | Table 3, KCP 0.16 (0.12-0.36) |
| `lk21` | log(0.82) 1/h | Table 3, KPC 0.82 (0.30-1.69) |
| `lkel` | log(0.32) 1/h at CRCL 120 mL/min | Table 3, Ke 0.32 (0.29-0.36), 'recalculated from rate per ml/min creatinine clearance' |
| `kel = exp(lkel) * CRCL / 120` | -- | Equation 2, `Ke = Kr * CrCl`; reference 120 mL/min = cohort mean (Methods) |
| `lfdepot` | log(1), held constant | Equation 3 'Fabs'; no value published (see Assumptions) |
| `etaiov_ka_*` | log(0.35^2 + 1) | Table 3, Ka BOV 35% |
| `etaiov_tlag_*` | log(0.75^2 + 1) | Table 3, Tlag BOV 75% |
| `etaiov_vc_*` | log(0.34^2 + 1) | Table 3, V BOV 34% |
| `etaiov_k12_*` | log(1.10^2 + 1) | Table 3, KCP BOV 110% |
| `etaiov_k21_*` | log(0.68^2 + 1) | Table 3, KPC BOV 68% |
| `etaiov_kel_*` | log(0.34^2 + 1) | Table 3, Ke BOV 34% |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | 0.02 mg/L, 0.0075 | Methods: assay SD = 0.02 + 0.0075 * concentration |
| `lambdaSd` | 0.2990 mg/L | Discussion 'Model uncertainties': lambda fitted by NPAG |
| Error = sqrt(SD^2 + lambda^2) | -- | Methods, 'error = (SD2 + Lambda2)0.5' |
| ODEs and `alag(depot)` | -- | Equation 3 |
| `Cc = central / vc` | -- | Equation 3, `concentration_blood = ammnt_blood / vol_blood` |

# Typical-value checks {#typical-value-checks}

These quantities follow from the parameters alone and are checked exactly.

```{r typical-checks}
p <- as.list(ui$theta)
ka <- exp(p$lka)
vc <- exp(p$lvc)
k12 <- exp(p$lk12)
k21 <- exp(p$lk21)
kel <- exp(p$lkel)
kr <- kel / 120

# Disposition eigenvalues of the two-compartment system.
sum_k <- k12 + k21 + kel
beta <- (sum_k - sqrt(sum_k^2 - 4 * k21 * kel)) / 2
alpha <- k21 * kel / beta
auc_closed <- 800 / (kel * vc)

# Pmetrics assay-error CV at 1 and 10 mg/L.
cv_assay <- (p$addSd + p$propSd * c(1, 10)) / c(1, 10)

checks <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Kr (1/h per mL/min)",
    "Assay-error CV at 1 mg/L (%)",
    "Assay-error CV at 10 mg/L (%)",
    "Clearance kel * V at CRCL 120 (L/h)",
    "Clearance kel * V at CRCL 120 (mL/min)",
    "Distribution half-life (h)",
    "Terminal half-life (h)",
    "AUC0-inf, 800 mg, F = 1 (mg*h/L)"
  ),
  Value = vapply(
    c(kr, 100 * cv_assay, kel * vc, kel * vc * 1000 / 60, log(2) / alpha, log(2) / beta, auc_closed),
    function(v) format(signif(v, 4), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
    character(1)
  ),
  Paper = c(
    "upper search bound 0.008",
    "2.75", "0.95",
    "--", "cohort CrCl mean 120",
    "--", "observed mean 8.24",
    "observed 62.4-64.5 (Table 2)"
  )
)
knitr::kable(checks, caption = "Derived typical values. Assay-error CV range from the Discussion ('a coefficient of variation between 2.75-0.95%').")

stopifnot(
  # Kr inside the Pmetrics search range (Methods: upper bound 0.008 h.ml-1).
  kr > 0, kr < 0.008,
  # The paper's own statement of the assay-error polynomial pins C0 and C1.
  abs(100 * cv_assay - c(2.75, 0.95)) < 0.005
)
```

The derived clearance is the first sign that the published medians do not form
a consistent model. Gabapentin is not metabolised and is eliminated unchanged
by the kidney, yet `kel * V` is 28.8 L/h (480 mL/min), four times the cohort's
mean creatinine clearance. The observed AUC0-inf of about 62 mg*h/L implies an
apparent clearance of about 12.9 L/h. Likewise, the micro-constants give a
terminal half-life of 2.8 h against the observed mean of 8.24 h.

A typical-value solve reproduces the closed-form AUC, which confirms the ODE
encoding:

```{r typical-solve}
grid <- c(0, seq(0.01, 120, by = 0.01))
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = grid,
  evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(grid) - 1)),
  amt = c(800, rep(0, length(grid) - 1)),
  cmt = c("depot", rep("central", length(grid) - 1)),
  OCC = 1L, CRCL = 120
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
auc_num <- sum(diff(typ$time) * (head(typ$Cc, -1) + tail(typ$Cc, -1)) / 2)
cat(sprintf(
  "Typical Cmax %.2f mg/L at %.2f h; AUC0-120 %.2f vs closed-form AUC0-inf %.2f mg*h/L\n",
  max(typ$Cc), typ$time[which.max(typ$Cc)], auc_num, auc_closed
))
# Same parameters on both sides, so only integration and trapezoid error
# separate them; the 120-h tail beyond is negligible at a 2.8-h half-life.
stopifnot(abs(auc_num / auc_closed - 1) < 0.002)
```

# Virtual cohort

A crossover cohort of 200 virtual volunteers receives all four formulations,
one 800 mg dose per period, sampled on the study schedule. Periods are 168 h
apart; the source does not state its washout, and at the model's half-life
there is no carry-over. The model has no formulation effect (the
per-formulation estimates are not published), so the four periods differ only
by the occasion draw. Creatinine clearance is normal around the cohort mean of
120 mL/min with an assumed SD of 25 mL/min, truncated to the observed 71.2-183.3
mL/min.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 200
period_h <- 168
sample_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48)

set.seed(20181023)
crcl <- numeric(0)
while (length(crcl) < n_sub) {
  draw <- rnorm(2 * n_sub, 120, 25)
  crcl <- c(crcl, draw[draw >= 71.2 & draw <= 183.3])
}
crcl <- crcl[seq_len(n_sub)]

dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), OCC = 1:4) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = (OCC - 1) * period_h, evid = 1L, amt = 800, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), OCC = 1:4, tad = sample_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = (OCC - 1) * period_h + tad, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::select(-tad)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CRCL = crcl[id]) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, OCC, CRCL)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(events),
  dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == n_sub,
  sum(events$evid == 1) == 4 * n_sub
)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20181023)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, events, returnType = "data.frame")
sim <- sim |>
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("OCC")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    OCC = as.integer(floor(time / period_h)) + 1L,
    tad_h = time - (OCC - 1) * period_h,
    formulation = paste("Formulation", OCC)
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(sim) == n_sub * 4 * length(sample_times),
  !anyNA(sim$Cc),
  all(sim$tad_h %in% sample_times)
)
```

## Visual predictive check (replicates Figure 3)

Figure 3 of Glerum 2018 overlays the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of 1000
simulations from the final NPAG distribution on the observed concentrations,
all four formulations pooled. The bands below are the same percentiles
simulated from the published medians (with residual error). The points are
the Figure 3 percentile lines, digitised by the maintainers where they are
not hidden by the observations.

```{r vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(tad_h > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad_h) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
fig3 <- data.frame(
  tad_h = c(8, 12, 24, 36, 12, 24, 36, 48, 12),
  value = c(2.65, 1.63, 0.40, 0.12, 4.29, 1.45, 0.63, 0.35, 0.17),
  percentile = c(rep("50th", 4), rep("95th", 4), "5th")
)
ggplot(vpc, aes(tad_h)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(data = fig3, aes(y = value, shape = percentile), colour = "firebrick", size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Gabapentin concentration (mg/L)",
    shape = "Figure 3\npercentile",
    caption = "Band: simulated 5th-95th percentiles; line: simulated median. Replicates Figure 3 of Glerum 2018."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-table}
vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(tad_h %in% c(8, 12, 24, 36, 48)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    fig3 |>
      dplyr::filter(percentile == "50th") |>
      dplyr::select(tad_h, fig3_median = value),
    by = "tad_h"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad_h,
    "Simulated 5th" = p05,
    "Simulated median" = p50,
    "Simulated 95th" = p95,
    "Figure 3 median (digitised)" = fig3_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated percentiles against the digitised Figure 3 median.")
```

The simulated median runs about a third below the paper's at 8 and 12 h, is
half of it at 24 h and is near zero by 36 h, where Figure 3 still shows about
0.1 mg/L. The upper band also decays much faster than Figure 3's. The lower
simulated percentiles go negative once concentrations fall below the 0.3 mg/L
additive process noise (lambda).

# Comparison with the observed NCA {#comparison-with-the-observed-nca}

NCA is run with PKNCA on the individual predictions (`Cc`, no residual error)
on the study schedule, one group per formulation. The reference is Glerum 2018
Table 2, NCA of the observed concentrations (means, and medians for Tmax).
`ncaComparisonTable()` summarises the simulated cohort by its median.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(conc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, formulation, time = tad_h, conc)
dose <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, formulation = paste("Formulation", OCC), time = 0, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | formulation + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | formulation + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(48, Inf),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"))
```

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  formulation = paste("Formulation", 1:4),
  cmax = c(5.33, 5.43, 5.48, 5.62),
  tmax = c(4.0, 4.25, 3.50, 3.75),
  auclast = c(63.42, 61.55, 61.16, 62.08),
  aucinf.obs = c(64.49, 62.39, 62.45, 63.03),
  half.life = c(8.12, 8.08, 9.08, 7.66)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_long,
  reference = reference,
  by = "formulation",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "mg*h/L", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Glerum 2018 Table 2 (observed) vs simulated cohort medians from the published",
    "Table 3 medians. AUC0-t is AUC over 0-48 h. * differs by more than 20%."
  )
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
ratio <- nca_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(formulation, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(reference, -formulation, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("formulation", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = sim / pub)
auc_ratio <- ratio$ratio[ratio$PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "aucinf.obs")]
cmax_ratio <- ratio$ratio[ratio$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
hl_ratio <- ratio$ratio[ratio$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]
# These pin the documented discrepancy of the published medians rather than
# agreement. AUC is set by dose / (kel * V) = 27.8 mg*h/L against about
# 62 observed, a ratio near 0.45 that cohort noise moves by a few percent; a
# mis-transcribed volume, rate constant or dose moves it far outside the band.
# The same holds for Cmax (typical 2.68 vs about 5.4 mg/L) and for the
# terminal half-life (about 2.8 h vs 8.2 h).
stopifnot(
  length(auc_ratio) == 8, length(cmax_ratio) == 4, length(hl_ratio) == 4,
  median(auc_ratio) > 0.35, median(auc_ratio) < 0.60,
  median(cmax_ratio) > 0.35, median(cmax_ratio) < 0.70,
  median(hl_ratio) > 0.20, median(hl_ratio) < 0.60
)
```

Every AUC and Cmax row is about half the observed value, and the simulated
half-life is less than half the observed one (about 3.7 h by NCA on the study
schedule, whose 12-48 h window still carries some of the distribution phase;
2.8 h from the micro-constants). Tmax is close. Table
2 also lists the NCA of each volunteer's Bayesian posterior predictions from
the final model (Cmax 4.87-5.16 mg/L, AUC0-inf 58.3-60.2 mg*h/L), which agree
with the observations. The full nonparametric model therefore fits the data;
it is the published summary of it that does not.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **The published medians do not reproduce the source's data.** At the cohort
  mean creatinine clearance, the Table 3 medians give a typical Cmax of 2.68
  mg/L, AUC0-inf of 27.8 mg*h/L and a terminal half-life of 2.8 h, against
  observed means of 5.3-5.6 mg/L, 62-64 mg*h/L and 7.7-9.1 h (Table 2).
  Implied clearance (28.8 L/h, 480 mL/min) is four times the mean creatinine
  clearance of a cohort whose drug is cleared unchanged by the kidney. No single
  value in Table 3 explains this. Raising Ke's reference creatinine clearance
  or lowering Ke to match AUC leaves the curve shape wrong against Figure 3,
  and halving V to match Cmax keeps the 2.8-h half-life. Marginal medians of a
  nonparametric joint distribution can differ from the median subject, but for
  roughly symmetric log-scale marginals the median of `Ke * V` is close to the
  product of the medians whatever their correlation, and the published
  between-occasion CVs of about 34% on both cannot produce a twofold gap.
  Nothing has been adjusted: the values are those printed. No erratum had been
  published as of November 2026, and the article has no supplementary material.
* **Unpublished parts of the final model.** The final model is a support-point
  distribution with every parameter estimated per formulation. Neither the
  distribution, the per-formulation estimates, the bioavailability `Fabs` nor
  `Kr` itself is published; only the pooled medians in Table 3. The package
  model therefore has no formulation effect.
* **Ke reference creatinine clearance.** Table 3 gives Ke 'recalculated from
  rate per ml/min creatinine clearance' without the creatinine clearance used.
  The cohort mean, 120 mL/min, is assumed, so `kel = 0.32 * CRCL / 120` and
  `Kr = 0.00267` per h per mL/min, inside the Pmetrics search range (upper
  bound 0.008).
* **Bioavailability.** Equation 3 multiplies the dose by `Fabs`, which is not
  given a value. The Discussion says F was not estimated, because it could not
  be separated from Ka without intravenous data. It is held at 1.
* **Equation 3 central-compartment term.** The printed central equation
  removes drug at `(KPC + Ke)` while the peripheral equation receives it at
  `KCP`. That pairing does not conserve mass and contradicts the Methods,
  which define KCP as the central-to-peripheral rate. The model uses KCP in
  both places. The printed pairing would lower exposure further (typical Cmax
  1.4 mg/L, AUC about 9 mg*h/L), and swapping the KCP and KPC labels leaves AUC
  unchanged, so neither alternative removes the discrepancy above.
* **Variability.** Table 3's between-occasion variability is the mean, over
  volunteers, of the CV of each volunteer's four per-period estimates. It is
  encoded as four-occasion inter-occasion variability with
  `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`, one occasion per crossover period. Because each
  period was a different formulation, it combines formulation and occasion
  effects, which the design cannot separate (Discussion). No between-subject
  variability is published, so the model has none; simulated variability
  between volunteers comes only from creatinine clearance. rxode2 warns that
  the per-occasion etas are not mu-referenced; this affects estimation, not
  simulation.
* **Residual error.** The Pmetrics lambda model,
  `SD = sqrt((0.02 + 0.0075 * C)^2 + 0.2990^2)`, is encoded directly as the
  standard deviation of an additive error. The assay polynomial was chosen by
  the authors from other gabapentin assays, so its coefficients are held
  constant; lambda was estimated.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** Weight on V (Equation 1) worsened
  the AIC by 25 and was dropped. Age, sex, race, height and serum creatinine
  were screened by regression only. These are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Virtual cohort.** Creatinine clearance is normal (mean 120, assumed SD 25
  mL/min) truncated to the observed range; the source reports only mean and
  range. Periods are 168 h apart. The NCA comparison uses simulated cohort
  medians against the source's means.
* **Figure 3 values** were digitised by the maintainers from the published
  image and are approximate (about +/-0.1 mg/L).
